examples.explanation: After concatenating all strings in chunks, s = "hello world hello". The words are "hello", "world", and "hello". The substring "wor" appears inside "world", but it is not a full word.

After concatenating all strings in chunks, s = "a-b a--b a-b". In "a-b", the hyphen is a joiner hyphen because it is between two lowercase English letters, so "a-b" is one word. In "a--b", neither hyphen is a joiner hyphen, so it is split into the words "a" and "b". Therefore, the words are "a-b", "a", "b", and "a-b".

After concatenating all strings in chunks, s = "-cat dog- mouse". The leading hyphen before "cat" and the trailing hyphen after "dog" are not joiner hyphens, so they are separators. The words are "cat", "dog", and "mouse".
